cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel, a prophet, with a message for the land of Israel. And friend, it does NOT open with small talk. God says, 'The end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.'

cards.question: God says the end has come upon the four corners of the land of Israel. What does that mean for the land?

answers.text: No part of it is left out
Only its borders are in danger
Only its capital is in danger

cards.text: God says the end is NOW upon them, and He will unleash His anger against them. I sat in a junk drawer for years waiting on 'someday,' and friend, this is not someday.

cards.question: God tells the land of Israel how He will judge them. He says He will judge them according to their own ___ and repay them for all their abominations.
God tells the land of Israel that He will look on them with pity and spare them.

cards.text: Then God says where all of this is headed. It comes down to what the people will finally know.

cards.question: When God punishes the land of Israel for its ways, what does He say the people will know?

cards.text: Then God announces a disaster and says it again: 'The end has come! The end has come!' That's an oven timer that will NOT stop beeping, friend, and you do not hit snooze on that one.

cards.question: What kind of disaster does God say is coming on the land of Israel?

cards.text: Doom has come to the people of the land. The time has come, the day is near, and up on the mountains, the sound has changed.

cards.question: As the day draws near, God says there is ___ on the mountains instead of shouts of joy.

cards.text: God repeats much of His warning and says it's coming very soon. But the closing line gets a little longer this time.

cards.question: In that longer closing line, what does God say the people will know about the blow that falls on them?

cards.text: God says, 'Behold, the day is here! It has come! Doom has gone out, the rod has budded, arrogance has bloomed.'

cards.question: God says the people's violence has grown into a rod. What is that rod for?
God says the people's wealth and their things of value will remain after the day comes.

cards.text: The day has arrived, and God talks about buying and selling. Mother Miller got me for a quarter, best deal of her life if you ask me, but here nobody gets to celebrate a deal.

cards.question: Why does God tell the buyer not to rejoice and the seller not to mourn?

answers.text: Wrath is on the whole multitude
Prices will soon go back up
The king will cancel every sale

cards.question: God says the vision about the whole multitude of Israel can still be taken back.

cards.text: The people blow the trumpet and make everything ready for battle. God says His wrath is upon the whole multitude.

cards.question: After the trumpet blows and everything is ready, the people march out to war.

cards.text: Everything's ready, and NOBODY goes. That's setting the alarm, laying out your clothes, and then lying there staring at the ceiling. Then God says the sword is outside, and plague and famine are within.

cards.question: With the sword outside and plague and famine within, who does God say will die by the sword?

cards.text: Some survivors escape and live in the mountains. God says they'll be moaning like doves of the valley.

cards.question: The survivors in the mountains moan, each one for his own ___.

cards.text: 'Every hand will go limp, and every knee will turn to water.' Friend, every time my old junk drawer rattled open, not knowing if it meant back to work or into the trash, I didn't even HAVE knees and they still turned to water.

cards.question: God says the people will put on sackcloth and shame will cover all their faces.

cards.text: Then they throw their silver into the streets, and their gold seems unclean. I watched people tear a junk drawer apart for ONE quarter, and these folks are tossing silver in the street.

cards.question: Why can't all that silver and gold help the people?

answers.text: It cannot save them that day
It is worth too little now

cards.text: God says, 'His beautiful ornaments they transformed into pride.' And then they made something out of them.

cards.question: What did the people fashion from those beautiful ornaments?
God says He will make those things unclean for the people and hand them over as plunder to ___.

cards.text: God says He will turn His face away, and violent men will enter His treasured place and defile it. Then He says, 'Forge the chain, for the land is full of crimes of bloodshed, and the city is full of violence.'

cards.question: With the land full of bloodshed, who does God say He will bring to take possession of the people's houses?

cards.text: God says they'll look for peace and find none. Disaster upon disaster comes, rumor after rumor, like a group chat that will NOT stop buzzing.

cards.question: With the rumors piling up, where do the people go looking for a vision?
When the people go looking for answers, God says counsel from the elders will still be there for them.

cards.text: The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed with despair, and the hands of the people will tremble. From the throne all the way down, nobody's steady.

cards.question: God's last word on how He will deal with them: He will judge them by their ___ standards.

findings.problem: The question adds 'own' to God's words ('according to their own ___'). BSB 7:3 just says 'your ways.' This added 'own' gives away the answer to Stop 2 card 20, which asks the baker to fill in 'own' in 'judge them by their ___ standards' (7:27).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke blends two everyday images. An oven timer that won't stop beeping is one picture. Hitting snooze belongs to an alarm clock, and oven timers don't have a snooze button.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The question says 'In that longer closing line,' which points back to card 12. The baker can no longer see card 12, so the question doesn't say which line it means.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Everything's ready, and NOBODY goes.' / 'That's setting the alarm...' / 'Then God says the sword is outside...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke compares the people to someone who won't get out of bed. That suggests they stay home out of inertia. But 7:14 gives the reason no one goes to war: 'for My wrath is upon the whole multitude.' The joke adds a reason the text doesn't give and makes light of people facing God's wrath.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: 'I watched people tear a junk drawer apart for ONE quarter' makes up a new event in Papa Dorin's drawer backstory. The backstory only mentions someone digging through for scissors or tape.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: A baker could argue for both wrong answers. For 'It is worth too little now': in 7:19 the silver is thrown into the streets and the gold seems unclean. For 'It has all been stolen': 7:21 says these things are handed over as plunder to foreigners. The right answer, 'It cannot save them that day,' also just restates the question ('why can't it help?') without giving a reason.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The question says 'those beautiful ornaments,' which points back to card 11. The baker can no longer see that card, so the question doesn't say whose ornaments or which ones.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question says 'those things,' which points back to the answer of card 12. It never names the ornaments and idols it means.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question says 'how He will deal with them' but never says who 'them' is: the king, the prince and the people of the land, from card 19.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
